preamble: Deaffrication of the postalveolar affricate [tʃ] to the voiceless palatal stop [c] is a regional realization rather than a widespread change. It is documented in Canary Islands and Cuban Spanish, where the traditional 'ch adherente' is articulated as a fully palatal stop, which voices to [ɟ] between vowels in line with the general intervocalic voicing of stops in these dialects. In the Canaries the plosive variant is still widespread, though it alternates with the standard affricate.

examples.note: Hualde (2014) gives Canarian/Cuban [mucáco] ~ [muɟáɟo]; the traditional Canarian 'ch adherente' is a palatal stop, and intervocalic voicing gives [ɟ].
